questions.q: Conserving the environment means
choices: using only the resources we need
questions.explain: Conserving the environment means using only the resources we need. This leaves enough resources for the future and reduces harm to the environment.
questions.lo: Explain the importance of conserving the environment

notes.1: People need some resources to live, such as water and food. Conservation is about using resources carefully, not stopping their use completely.
notes.2: Replacing forests with farms destroys habitats. Conservation aims to protect the environment, so think about how resources should be used.
notes.3: Conservation covers all resources, such as water, soil, energy and forests, not only endangered animals. Think about how resources should be used.

questions.q: Why is fresh water a limited resource?
choices: most of Earth's water is fresh
fresh water is only found in ice
fresh water cannot be cleaned and reused
less than 1% of Earth's water is fresh and easy to use
questions.explain: Most of Earth's water is salty seawater. Less than 1% of all the water on Earth is fresh water that is easily available for people to use.
questions.lo: Explain the importance of conserving the environment

notes.0: Most of Earth's water is in the oceans, and it is salty. Only a very small fraction is fresh.
notes.1: Fresh water is also found in rivers, lakes and underground. It is the small amount of fresh water that makes it limited.
notes.2: Used water can be treated and reused, as NEWater in Singapore shows. It is the small amount of usable fresh water on Earth that makes it limited.

why.right: Fresh water is limited because most of Earth's water is salty seawater that people cannot drink.
wrong: Fresh water is limited because rainwater is salty until it flows into a river.
Fresh water is limited because plants use up most of the water that falls as rain.

questions.q: Which action reduces the use of fossil fuels?
choices: planting more trees in the garden
leaving the lights on all day
taking public transport instead of a car
questions.explain: A bus or train carries many people at once, so it uses less fuel per person than a car. Taking public transport reduces the burning of fossil fuels.
questions.lo: Identify how an action helps to conserve the environment

notes.0: Trees take in carbon dioxide, but planting them does not reduce how much fossil fuel is burnt. Look for an action that uses less fuel.
notes.1: Leaving lights on wastes electricity, and most electricity comes from burning fossil fuels. Look for an action that uses less fuel.
notes.3: Driving burns petrol, which is a fossil fuel. Think about a way of travelling that uses less fuel per person.

why.right: Public transport saves fossil fuels because one vehicle carries many people, so less fuel is burnt per person.
wrong: Public transport saves fossil fuels because buses and trains run without using any energy.
Public transport saves fossil fuels because buses give out oxygen instead of carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Which action most directly reduces deforestation?
questions.explain: Paper is made from wood, which comes from trees. Using less paper means fewer trees need to be cut down.
questions.lo: Identify how an action helps to conserve the environment

notes.0: Public transport saves fuel, but it does not directly stop trees from being cut down. Think about which product is made from trees.
notes.2: Switching off the fan saves electricity, but it is not directly linked to cutting down trees. Think about what is made from wood.
notes.3: Plastic bottles are made from crude oil, not trees. Recycling them saves oil, but think about which product is made from wood.

why.right: Using less paper reduces deforestation because paper is made from wood pulp taken from trees.
wrong: Using less paper reduces deforestation because paper is made from plastic that harms trees.
Using less paper reduces deforestation because paper is made from the leaves trees need for food.

questions.q: Reforestation reduces carbon dioxide in the air because trees
choices: give out carbon dioxide for photosynthesis
take in carbon dioxide for photosynthesis
questions.explain: Trees take in carbon dioxide from the air for photosynthesis. Planting more trees removes more carbon dioxide from the air.
questions.lo: Identify how an action helps to conserve the environment

notes.0: Photosynthesis uses up carbon dioxide rather than giving it out. Think about which way the gas moves during photosynthesis.
notes.2: Respiration releases energy, but this does not remove carbon dioxide from the air. Focus on the process that uses carbon dioxide.
notes.3: Photosynthesis gives out oxygen rather than taking it in. Think about which gas leaves take in to make food.

why.right: Trees reduce carbon dioxide because they use it with water to make glucose in photosynthesis.
wrong: Trees reduce carbon dioxide because they change it into oxygen during respiration.
Trees reduce carbon dioxide because they store it as a gas inside their trunks.

questions.q: Composting food waste reduces greenhouse gases because
choices: more waste needs to be burnt
less waste needs to be burnt
compost releases oxygen as it breaks down
questions.explain: Burning waste gives off carbon dioxide. Composting food waste means less waste needs to be burnt, so less greenhouse gas is released.
questions.lo: Identify how an action helps to conserve the environment

notes.0: Burning more waste would release more carbon dioxide, which is a greenhouse gas. Think about how composting changes the amount of waste burnt.
notes.1: Compost does not absorb all the carbon dioxide in the air. Think about what happens to food waste that is not composted.
notes.3: Decomposers use up oxygen as they break down compost and give off carbon dioxide. Think about what happens to food waste that is not composted.

why.right: Composting reduces greenhouse gases because composted waste is not burnt to give off carbon dioxide.
wrong: Composting reduces greenhouse gases because compost takes in all the carbon dioxide from the air.
Composting reduces greenhouse gases because composted waste turns into oxygen as it breaks down.

questions.q: The place where an organism lives is its
questions.explain: A habitat is the place where an organism lives. It provides the organism with food, water and shelter.
questions.lo: Name physical factors of a habitat and the instruments used to measure them

notes.1: A community is all the populations of different organisms living in one place. The question asks about the place itself.
notes.2: A population is a group of organisms of the same kind. The question asks about the place where an organism lives.
notes.3: A food chain shows the feeding relationships between organisms. It is not a place.

questions.q: Which is a physical factor of an environment?
questions.explain: Physical factors are the non-living parts of an environment, such as light intensity, temperature and pH. Light intensity is a physical factor.
questions.lo: Name physical factors of a habitat and the instruments used to measure them

notes.0: Prey are living organisms, so the type of prey is a living factor. Look for a non-living part of the environment.
notes.1: Predators are living organisms. Look for a factor that is not a living thing.
notes.2: Parasites are living organisms. Look for a factor that can be measured with an instrument, such as a probe.

why.right: Light intensity is a physical factor because it is a non-living part of the environment.
wrong: Light intensity is a physical factor because it is made by the living plants in a habitat.
Light intensity is a physical factor because it can only be seen and never measured.

questions.q: A student compares the acidity of two ponds. Which should she use?
choices: a temperature probe with a data logger
a light probe with a data logger
a pH probe with a data logger
questions.explain: Acidity is measured as pH. A pH probe with a data logger measures and records the pH of each pond.
questions.lo: Name physical factors of a habitat and the instruments used to measure them

notes.0: A temperature probe measures how hot or cold the water is, not its acidity. Think about the scale used to measure acidity.
notes.1: A light probe measures light intensity, not acidity. Think about the scale used to measure acidity.
notes.2: A measuring cylinder measures volume. The amount of water says nothing about how acidic it is.

why.right: A pH probe is used for the ponds because acidity is measured on the pH scale.
wrong: A pH probe is used for the ponds because acidity depends on how much water there is.
A pH probe is used for the ponds because acidic water is always warmer than other water.

questions.q: A student compares how bright two parts of a forest are. Which should he use?
choices: a pH probe with a data logger
a light probe with a data logger
a temperature probe with a data logger
questions.explain: Brightness is light intensity. A light probe with a data logger measures and records the light intensity in each part of the forest.
questions.lo: Name physical factors of a habitat and the instruments used to measure them

notes.0: A pH probe measures how acidic or alkaline something is, not how bright it is. Think about which factor brightness describes.
notes.1: A measuring cylinder measures volume, not brightness. Think about which factor brightness describes.
notes.3: A temperature probe measures how hot or cold it is. A bright place is not always a warmer place, so brightness needs its own measurement.

why.right: A light probe is used in the forest because brightness is measured as light intensity.
wrong: A light probe is used in the forest because brightness is measured as the temperature of the air.
A light probe is used in the forest because brightness depends on the pH of the soil.

questions.q: Why are few organisms found in hot deserts?
choices: extreme temperatures and lack of water
questions.explain: Hot deserts have very high daytime temperatures and very little water. Few organisms can survive these conditions.
questions.lo: Explain the importance of physical factors to the survival of organisms

notes.1: Soil rich in minerals would help plants grow, not stop them. Think about the temperature and water in a hot desert.
notes.2: Hot deserts get plenty of strong sunlight. Think about what deserts lack.
notes.3: Hot deserts get very little rainfall. Think about how water and temperature affect living things there.

why.right: Few organisms live in hot deserts because most cannot survive the extreme heat and lack of water.
wrong: Few organisms live in hot deserts because the strong sunlight stops all photosynthesis.
Few organisms live in hot deserts because the sand contains too many minerals for plants.

questions.q: Suitable physical factors let plants grow. How does this help animals?
choices: plants give out carbon dioxide for animals to breathe
questions.explain: Plants are food for herbivores and provide shelter for many animals. When physical factors let plants grow, animals have more food and places to live.
questions.lo: Explain the importance of physical factors to the survival of organisms

notes.0: Animals do not depend on plants for heat. Think about what animals get by eating plants or living among them.
notes.2: Plants take in minerals from the soil. They do not produce minerals for animals.
notes.3: Animals breathe in oxygen, not carbon dioxide. Think about what plants give to the animals that feed or hide among them.

why.right: Plant growth helps animals because plants are food for herbivores and give animals shelter.
wrong: Plant growth helps animals because plants give out the heat energy animals need to stay warm.
Plant growth helps animals because plants make the minerals that animals need to grow.

questions.q: Cold desert plants have shallow roots. Which condition explains this?
choices: the soil is deep and warm
only a thin soil layer is ice-free
questions.explain: In cold deserts, the soil below a thin top layer stays frozen all year. Roots can only grow in the thin layer that thaws, so they are shallow.
questions.lo: Explain the importance of physical factors to the survival of organisms

notes.0: Cold deserts get very little rainfall. Think about what lies beneath the surface of the soil.
notes.1: The soil in cold deserts is cold, not warm, and much of it stays frozen. Think about how deep roots can grow.
notes.3: Soil acidity does not explain shallow roots here. Think about what happens to the deeper soil in very cold places.

why.right: Cold desert plants have shallow roots because the soil below a thin top layer stays frozen.
wrong: Cold desert plants have shallow roots because frequent rain keeps the surface soil very wet.
Cold desert plants have shallow roots because deep soil is too warm for roots to grow.

questions.q: A structural adaptation is
choices: a physical factor of the habitat
a physical characteristic that helps survival
questions.explain: A structural adaptation is a physical feature of an organism's body that helps it survive, such as thick fur or waxy leaves.
questions.lo: Classify adaptations as structural or behavioural

notes.0: A physical factor, such as temperature or light, is part of the habitat. An adaptation is a feature of the organism itself.
notes.2: A change in the habitat is not something the organism has. An adaptation belongs to the organism.
notes.3: A behaviour that helps survival is a behavioural adaptation. Structural adaptations are about the body itself.

questions.q: A pangolin curls into a ball when attacked. This adaptation is
questions.explain: Curling into a ball is something the pangolin does, so it is a behaviour. It helps the pangolin survive attacks, so it is a behavioural adaptation.
questions.lo: Classify adaptations as structural or behavioural

notes.1: A structural adaptation is a feature of the body, such as scales. Curling up is something the pangolin does.
notes.2: Curling into a ball protects the pangolin from predators, so it does help it survive.

why.right: Curling into a ball is a behavioural adaptation because it is an action that helps the pangolin survive.
wrong: Curling into a ball is a behavioural adaptation because it is a body part that helps the pangolin survive.
Curling into a ball is a behavioural adaptation because it changes the shape of the pangolin's scales.

questions.q: A waxplant has waxy leaves that reduce water loss. This adaptation is
questions.explain: Waxy leaves are a physical feature of the plant. They reduce water loss and help the plant survive, so this is a structural adaptation.
questions.lo: Classify adaptations as structural or behavioural

notes.0: Waxy leaves reduce water loss, which helps the plant survive. That makes them an adaptation.
notes.2: A behavioural adaptation is an action. Waxy leaves are part of the plant's body.

why.right: Waxy leaves are a structural adaptation because they are a body feature that helps the plant survive.
wrong: Waxy leaves are a structural adaptation because they are an action that helps the plant survive.
Waxy leaves are a structural adaptation because the plant grows them only on hot days.

questions.q: A mudskipper digs burrows to keep itself cool. This adaptation is
questions.explain: Digging burrows is something the mudskipper does. It helps the mudskipper keep cool and survive, so it is a behavioural adaptation.
questions.lo: Classify adaptations as structural or behavioural

notes.0: Keeping cool helps the mudskipper survive, so digging burrows is an adaptation.
notes.1: A structural adaptation is a feature of the body. Digging is something the mudskipper does.

why.right: Digging burrows is a behavioural adaptation because it is an action that helps the mudskipper survive.
wrong: Digging burrows is a behavioural adaptation because the burrow is part of the mudskipper's body.
Digging burrows is a behavioural adaptation because it changes the mudskipper's body to keep it cool.

questions.q: A crocodile has scales that protect it from heat and injury. This adaptation is
questions.explain: Scales are part of the crocodile's body. They protect it from heat and injury, so they are a structural adaptation.
questions.lo: Classify adaptations as structural or behavioural

notes.1: Scales protect the crocodile from heat and injury, which helps it survive. That makes them an adaptation.
notes.2: A behavioural adaptation is an action. Scales are part of the crocodile's body.

why.right: Scales are a structural adaptation because they are a body feature that helps the crocodile survive.
wrong: Scales are a structural adaptation because they are an action that helps the crocodile survive.
Scales are a structural adaptation because the crocodile grows them only when it is attacked.

questions.q: Which is a behavioural adaptation?
choices: a mangrove tree has breathing roots
a pangolin has a long, sticky tongue
a mangrove snail has a thick shell
a king cobra hunts at dawn or dusk
questions.explain: Hunting at dawn or dusk is something the king cobra does, so it is a behavioural adaptation. The other options are body features, which are structural adaptations.
questions.lo: Classify adaptations as structural or behavioural

notes.0: Breathing roots are part of the mangrove tree's body, so they are a structural adaptation. Look for an action.
notes.1: A long, sticky tongue is part of the pangolin's body. Look for something an organism does.
notes.2: A thick shell is part of the snail's body. Look for something an organism does.

why.right: Hunting at dawn or dusk is a behavioural adaptation because it is something the cobra does.
wrong: Hunting at dawn or dusk is a behavioural adaptation because it is a part of the cobra's body.
Hunting at dawn or dusk is a behavioural adaptation because it changes the shape of the cobra's eyes.

questions.q: The buttress roots of a rainforest tree help it to
choices: take in minerals near the soil surface
questions.explain: In a rainforest, most minerals are in the top layer of soil. Buttress roots spread out widely near the surface to take in these minerals. They also help support the tall tree.
questions.lo: Explain how an adaptive trait helps an organism survive

notes.0: Buttress roots are not used to store water. Rainforests have plenty of rain, so think about what the roots spread out to reach.
notes.1: Removing salt is an adaptation of mangrove plants, which live in seawater. Rainforest trees grow in soil.
notes.2: Roots grow at the base of the tree and do not trap sunlight. Think about what roots take in from the soil.

why.right: Buttress roots spread widely near the surface because most minerals in rainforest soil are found there.
wrong: Buttress roots spread widely near the surface because they need to trap sunlight for photosynthesis.
Buttress roots spread widely near the surface because rainforest soil has no water deep down.

questions.q: A moth's brown colour matches tree bark. This helps it to
questions.explain: The brown colour blends in with the tree bark. This camouflage makes the moth hard for predators to see.
questions.lo: Explain how an adaptive trait helps an organism survive

notes.0: Moths do not make food from sunlight. Think about why matching the colour of the bark would be useful.
notes.1: Blending into the bark makes the moth harder to see, which would not help to attract a mate. Think about who it is hiding from.
notes.3: Matching the bark does not change the moth's temperature. Think about why being hard to see would help.

why.right: Brown colour helps the moth because it blends in with the bark, so predators find it hard to see.
wrong: Brown colour helps the moth because brown absorbs sunlight to make food for the moth.
Brown colour helps the moth because brown colours make the moth taste bad to predators.

questions.q: A rainforest tree grows very tall. This helps its leaves to
questions.explain: In a rainforest, many plants compete for light. A tall tree raises its leaves above other plants, so they trap more sunlight for photosynthesis.
questions.lo: Explain how an adaptive trait helps an organism survive

notes.0: Rainforests are wet, so reducing water loss is not the main problem. Think about what the leaves reach by being high up.
notes.1: Minerals are taken in by the roots, not the leaves. Think about what the leaves reach by being high up.
notes.2: Oxygen is plentiful in the air at all heights. Think about what is shaded out lower down in a forest.

why.right: Growing tall helps the tree because its leaves rise above other plants to get more sunlight.
wrong: Growing tall helps the tree because the air higher up has more oxygen for photosynthesis.
Growing tall helps the tree because its leaves can take in minerals from the air.

questions.q: A mangrove snail releases mucus to cling to trees. This helps it to
choices: avoid being washed away at high tide
questions.explain: Mangroves are flooded by the tide. The mucus helps the snail stick to the tree so it is not washed away when the tide comes in.
questions.lo: Explain how an adaptive trait helps an organism survive

notes.0: The mucus is used to stick to the tree, not to remove salt. Think about what happens in a mangrove when the tide rises.
notes.2: The mucus is used for clinging, not for keeping gills damp. Think about the danger when the tide rises.
notes.3: Clinging to a tree does not help the snail catch prey. Think about the danger when the tide rises.

why.right: Clinging with mucus helps the snail because it stays attached to the tree when the rising tide flows past.
wrong: Clinging with mucus helps the snail because the mucus removes salt from the seawater around it.
Clinging with mucus helps the snail because the mucus traps sunlight to make food for it.

questions.q: Adaptive traits in organisms develop
questions.explain: Adaptive traits are passed from parents to offspring. They become common in a population slowly, over many generations.
questions.lo: Explain how an adaptive trait helps an organism survive

notes.1: Organisms cannot grow new traits right after a change. Traits are passed on from parents to offspring.
notes.2: One generation is far too short. Traits become common only as they are passed on again and again.
notes.3: A few days is far too short for traits to develop. Think about how traits are passed from parents to offspring.

why.right: Adaptive traits take many generations because organisms with useful traits survive and pass them to their offspring.
wrong: Adaptive traits take many generations because each organism slowly changes its body as it gets older.
Adaptive traits take many generations because organisms must first decide which traits they want.

questions.q: When conditions change, organisms that cannot survive the new conditions will
questions.explain: Organisms without the traits needed for the new conditions cannot survive them, so they die. Only those with suitable traits survive and reproduce.
questions.lo: Predict how a change in environmental conditions affects survival

notes.0: Organisms cannot develop new traits at once when conditions change. Traits develop only over many generations.
notes.1: Organisms struggling to survive do not reproduce more. Think about what happens to organisms that cannot cope.
notes.3: Organisms that cannot cope with the new conditions become fewer, not more common. Think about what happens to organisms that cannot survive.

why.right: Organisms that cannot survive new conditions die because they lack the traits needed to cope with them.
wrong: Organisms that cannot survive new conditions die because they grow new traits too quickly.
Organisms that cannot survive new conditions die because they use up their food faster than before.

questions.q: A crab is adapted to clean, oxygen-rich streams. These streams are decreasing. Its population will
questions.explain: The crab is adapted only to clean, oxygen-rich streams. As these habitats decrease, fewer crabs can survive, so the population decreases.
questions.lo: Predict how a change in environmental conditions affects survival

notes.1: The crab depends on a habitat that is shrinking. Fewer suitable streams means the population cannot stay the same.
notes.2: The crab's habitat is getting smaller, not larger. Fewer suitable streams cannot support more crabs.

why.right: The crab population decreases because fewer crabs can find the clean, oxygen-rich streams they are adapted to.
wrong: The crab population decreases because the crabs quickly adapt to live in dirty water instead.
The crab population decreases because crabs make the streams dirty as their numbers grow.

questions.q: Rising temperatures make mosquito eggs hatch faster. The mosquito population will
questions.explain: Warmer temperatures make the eggs hatch faster, so more mosquitoes are produced in a shorter time. The population increases.
questions.lo: Predict how a change in environmental conditions affects survival

notes.0: Faster hatching means more young mosquitoes are produced in the same time. That changes the population size.
notes.2: Eggs hatching faster does not kill mosquitoes. Think about how faster hatching affects the number of mosquitoes.

why.right: The mosquito population increases because faster hatching produces more young mosquitoes in the same time.
wrong: The mosquito population increases because warmer temperatures stop adult mosquitoes from ever dying.
The mosquito population increases because each egg hatches into many mosquitoes in warm weather.

questions.q: Which animal has the highest chance of survival if one food source disappears?
choices: one that eats only gum leaves
one that eats many kinds of food
questions.explain: An animal that eats many kinds of food can switch to another food if one source disappears. An animal that eats only one food would have nothing to eat.
questions.lo: Predict how a change in environmental conditions affects survival

notes.0: An animal that eats only bamboo has no other food if the bamboo disappears. Think about which diet gives a backup.
notes.1: An animal that eats only gum leaves depends on one food. If that food disappears, it would struggle to survive.
notes.2: An animal that eats only milkweed depends on one food. Think about which animal could switch to something else.

why.right: An animal with a varied diet survives better because it can switch to other food when one disappears.
wrong: An animal with a varied diet survives better because it does not need to eat as often.
An animal with a varied diet survives better because it can make its own food when needed.

questions.q: Organisms of the same kind living in the same environment form a
questions.explain: A population is a group of organisms of the same kind living in the same place at the same time.
questions.lo: Classify a group as an organism, population, community or ecosystem

notes.0: A community is made up of different kinds of organisms living together. The question describes only one kind.
notes.1: An ecosystem includes all the organisms and their physical environment. The question describes only organisms of one kind.
notes.3: A habitat is the place where an organism lives. The question describes a group of organisms.

questions.q: An ecosystem is made up of
choices: a community and its physical environment
questions.explain: An ecosystem is a community of organisms together with the physical environment they live in, such as water, light and soil.
questions.lo: Classify a group as an organism, population, community or ecosystem

notes.0: A community is only the living part. An ecosystem also includes the non-living surroundings.
notes.1: One population is only one kind of organism. An ecosystem includes all the kinds living there, as well as their surroundings.
notes.2: The physical environment is only the non-living part. An ecosystem also includes the living organisms.

questions.q: All the frogs in a pond are a
questions.explain: All the frogs are organisms of the same kind living in the same pond, so they form a population.
questions.lo: Classify a group as an organism, population, community or ecosystem

notes.0: An ecosystem includes all the organisms and the physical environment. Here only one kind of organism is described.
notes.2: A community includes different kinds of organisms. All the frogs are only one kind.
notes.3: An organism is one single living thing. Here there are many frogs.

why.right: All the frogs in a pond are a population because they are one kind of organism living in one place.
wrong: All the frogs in a pond are a population because they include different kinds of organisms.
All the frogs in a pond are a population because they include the water and plants around them.

questions.q: All the fish, plants and snails living in a pond are a
questions.explain: Fish, plants and snails are different kinds of organisms living in the same pond. Together they form a community.
questions.lo: Classify a group as an organism, population, community or ecosystem

notes.1: An ecosystem also includes the non-living parts, such as water and light. Here only the living things are described.
notes.2: A population is only one kind of organism. Here there are several kinds.
notes.3: An organism is a single living thing. Here there are many different organisms.

why.right: The fish, plants and snails are a community because they are different populations living in one place.
wrong: The fish, plants and snails are a community because they are all the same kind of organism.
The fish, plants and snails are a community because they include the water and light in the pond.

questions.q: The pond organisms together with the water, light and temperature form
questions.explain: The pond organisms form a community. A community together with its physical environment, such as water, light and temperature, is an ecosystem.
questions.lo: Classify a group as an organism, population, community or ecosystem

notes.1: An organism is a single living thing. Water, light and temperature are not living things.
notes.2: A population is one kind of organism. Here there are many organisms as well as non-living factors.
notes.3: A community is only the living organisms. Water, light and temperature are non-living parts that are also included here.

why.right: The pond and its organisms form an ecosystem because it includes the community and its physical environment.
wrong: The pond and its organisms form an ecosystem because it includes only one kind of organism.
The pond and its organisms form an ecosystem because it includes only the living things in the pond.

questions.q: Which is an example of a community?
choices: all the mudskippers in a mangrove
all the plants and animals in a mangrove
questions.explain: A community is all the populations of different organisms living in the same place. All the plants and animals in a mangrove form a community.
questions.lo: Classify a group as an organism, population, community or ecosystem

notes.0: All the mudskippers are only one kind of organism, so they form a population. A community has many kinds.
notes.1: Seawater is a non-living part of the mangrove. A community is made up of living things.
notes.2: One tree is a single organism. A community has many organisms of different kinds.

why.right: The plants and animals in a mangrove are a community because they are different populations living together.
wrong: The plants and animals in a mangrove are a community because they are all one kind of organism.
The plants and animals in a mangrove are a community because they include the seawater and mud.

questions.q: A relationship in which both organisms benefit is
questions.explain: Mutualism is a relationship between two organisms in which both benefit.
questions.lo: Identify predator-prey, mutualism and parasitism relationships

notes.0: In parasitism, only the parasite benefits and the host is harmed. The question describes both organisms benefiting.
notes.1: In a predator-prey relationship, the predator benefits but the prey is eaten. Both do not benefit.

questions.q: A parasite
choices: harms its host without killing it
questions.explain: A parasite lives on or in another organism, called the host, and takes food from it. It harms the host but usually does not kill it.
questions.lo: Identify predator-prey, mutualism and parasitism relationships

notes.0: Killing prey for food describes a predator. A parasite feeds on its host while the host stays alive.
notes.2: When both organisms benefit, the relationship is mutualism. A parasite gives nothing useful back to its host.
notes.3: Making their own food is what producers do. A parasite takes its food from another organism.

questions.q: Ants protect scale insects and feed on their sugary solution. This is
questions.explain: The ants get food from the sugary solution, and the scale insects get protection. Both benefit, so this is mutualism.
questions.lo: Identify predator-prey, mutualism and parasitism relationships

notes.0: The ants do not kill and eat the scale insects. They protect them and feed on what the insects make.
notes.1: Neither organism is harmed here. Look at what each organism gets from the other.

why.right: The ants and scale insects show mutualism because the ants get food and the insects get protection.
wrong: The ants and scale insects show mutualism because the ants kill and eat the scale insects.
The ants and scale insects show mutualism because the ants harm the insects without killing them.

questions.q: Roundworms live in human intestines and take food from them. This is
questions.explain: The roundworms benefit by taking food from the human host. The human is harmed but is not killed, so this is parasitism.
questions.lo: Identify predator-prey, mutualism and parasitism relationships

notes.0: The human gains nothing from the roundworms and loses food. Both organisms do not benefit.
notes.2: The roundworms do not kill and eat the human. They live inside the host and take its food.

why.right: Roundworms in the intestines are parasites because they take food from the human and harm the host.
wrong: Roundworms in the intestines are parasites because they help the human digest food in return.
Roundworms in the intestines are parasites because they kill the human and then eat it.

questions.q: A sea eagle catches and eats fish. This is
questions.explain: The sea eagle kills and eats the fish. The sea eagle is the predator and the fish is the prey.
questions.lo: Identify predator-prey, mutualism and parasitism relationships

notes.1: A parasite feeds on a living host without killing it. The fish here is caught and eaten.
notes.2: In mutualism both organisms benefit. The fish does not benefit from being eaten.

why.right: The sea eagle and the fish are predator and prey because the eagle kills and eats the fish.
wrong: The sea eagle and the fish are predator and prey because both of them benefit.
The sea eagle and the fish are predator and prey because the eagle lives inside the fish.

questions.q: A sea anemone protects a clownfish and eats fish the clownfish attracts. This is
questions.explain: The clownfish gets protection from the sea anemone, and the sea anemone gets food from the fish the clownfish attracts. Both benefit, so this is mutualism.
questions.lo: Identify predator-prey, mutualism and parasitism relationships

notes.0: Neither organism is harmed here. Look at what each one gains from the other.
notes.2: The sea anemone does not eat the clownfish. It eats other fish, and the clownfish is protected.

why.right: The sea anemone and clownfish show mutualism because each one gains something from the other.
wrong: The sea anemone and clownfish show mutualism because the anemone kills and eats the clownfish.
The sea anemone and clownfish show mutualism because the clownfish harms the anemone without killing it.

questions.q: A stable ecosystem results when
choices: all interrelationships between organisms are maintained
questions.explain: Organisms in an ecosystem depend on one another. When all these interrelationships are kept, population numbers stay balanced and the ecosystem is stable.
questions.lo: Predict how removing an organism affects a stable ecosystem

notes.0: Removing a predator lets its prey increase out of control. This upsets the balance of the ecosystem.
notes.1: Without decomposers, dead matter builds up and nutrients are not returned to the soil. The ecosystem would become unbalanced.
notes.2: If herbivores keep increasing, they will eat too many plants. Think about what keeps numbers in balance.

why.right: An ecosystem stays stable when relationships are kept because each population keeps the numbers of others in balance.
wrong: An ecosystem stays stable when relationships are kept because every population then keeps increasing.
An ecosystem stays stable when relationships are kept because the organisms stop feeding on each other.

questions.q: Wolves that eat elk are removed from a park. The number of elk will
questions.explain: Wolves eat elk. Without wolves, fewer elk are killed, so the number of elk increases.
questions.lo: Predict how removing an organism affects a stable ecosystem

notes.0: Removing the predator changes how many elk are eaten. That affects the number of elk.
notes.1: Wolves are predators of elk. Removing them means fewer elk are eaten, not more.

why.right: The elk increase because their predator is gone, so fewer elk are killed and eaten.
wrong: The elk increase because the wolves were competing with the elk for plants.
The elk increase because the wolves were parasites that made the elk ill.

questions.q: More elk eat more plants. Beavers also eat these plants. Beaver numbers will
questions.explain: Elk and beavers eat the same plants. If elk eat more of the plants, less food is left for beavers, so beaver numbers decrease.
questions.lo: Predict how removing an organism affects a stable ecosystem

notes.1: Elk and beavers compete for the same plants. When elk eat more, the beavers' food supply changes.
notes.2: More elk eating the plants leaves less food for the beavers. Less food cannot support more beavers.

why.right: Beaver numbers decrease because elk and beavers compete for the same plants, leaving less food for beavers.
wrong: Beaver numbers decrease because elk are predators that hunt and eat beavers.
Beaver numbers decrease because beavers are parasites that depend on living inside elk.

questions.q: In grass --> grasshopper --> frog, all the frogs are removed. Grasshoppers will at first
questions.explain: Frogs eat grasshoppers. When all the frogs are removed, fewer grasshoppers are eaten, so their numbers increase at first.
questions.lo: Predict how removing an organism affects a stable ecosystem

notes.0: Frogs are the predators of grasshoppers. Removing them means fewer grasshoppers are eaten.
notes.2: Removing the frogs changes how many grasshoppers are eaten. That affects the number of grasshoppers.

why.right: Grasshoppers increase at first because their predator is gone, so fewer of them are eaten.
wrong: Grasshoppers increase at first because the frogs were eating the grass that grasshoppers need.
Grasshoppers increase at first because the grasshoppers can now feed on the frogs.

questions.q: Green plants are producers because they
questions.explain: Green plants make their own food by photosynthesis, using light energy. Organisms that make their own food are producers.
questions.lo: Identify producers and consumers in a food chain

notes.0: Green plants do not feed on animals. Think about how plants get their food.
notes.1: Organisms that eat other organisms are consumers. Plants get their food in a different way.
notes.2: Breaking down dead matter is what decomposers do. Think about the process that happens in green leaves.

why.right: Green plants are producers because they use light energy to make glucose by photosynthesis.
wrong: Green plants are producers because they take in ready-made food from the soil.
Green plants are producers because they break down dead matter to make their food.

questions.q: In rice plant --> grasshopper --> frog --> snake, which is the primary consumer?
questions.explain: The primary consumer is the first consumer in a food chain. It eats the producer. Here the grasshopper eats the rice plant.
questions.lo: Identify producers and consumers in a food chain

notes.0: The frog eats the grasshopper, so it is the second consumer. Look for the organism that eats the producer.
notes.1: The rice plant makes its own food, so it is the producer, not a consumer.
notes.2: The snake is at the end of the chain. Look for the organism that eats the producer directly.

why.right: The grasshopper is the primary consumer because it is the first organism to feed on the producer.
wrong: The grasshopper is the primary consumer because it makes its own food from sunlight.
The grasshopper is the primary consumer because it is eaten by the producer.

questions.q: In rice plant --> grasshopper --> frog --> snake, which is the secondary consumer?
questions.explain: The secondary consumer eats the primary consumer. The frog eats the grasshopper, so it is the secondary consumer.
questions.lo: Identify producers and consumers in a food chain

notes.0: The snake eats the frog, so it is one level further along. Look for the organism that eats the primary consumer.
notes.1: The rice plant is the producer, not a consumer.
notes.3: The grasshopper eats the producer, so it is the primary consumer. Look one step further along the chain.

why.right: The frog is the secondary consumer because it feeds on the primary consumer, the grasshopper.
wrong: The frog is the secondary consumer because it feeds directly on the rice plant.
The frog is the secondary consumer because it is the second largest organism in the chain.

questions.q: In rice plant --> grasshopper --> frog --> snake, which is the tertiary consumer?
questions.explain: The tertiary consumer eats the secondary consumer. The snake eats the frog, so it is the tertiary consumer.
questions.lo: Identify producers and consumers in a food chain

notes.1: The rice plant is the producer. It makes its own food and is not a consumer.
notes.2: The grasshopper eats the producer, so it is the primary consumer. Count along the chain to the third consumer.
notes.3: The frog eats the primary consumer, so it is the secondary consumer. Look one step further along the chain.

why.right: The snake is the tertiary consumer because it feeds on the secondary consumer, the frog.
wrong: The snake is the tertiary consumer because it feeds directly on the grasshopper.
The snake is the tertiary consumer because it is the largest animal in the chain.

questions.q: In which food chain is the frog a secondary consumer?
questions.explain: A food chain starts with the producer, and each arrow points to the organism that eats. When the frog eats an insect that ate a plant, the frog is the secondary consumer.
questions.lo: Identify producers and consumers in a food chain

notes.0: This chain starts with the frog, but a food chain must start with a producer. The arrows show the direction food passes.
notes.1: Here the frog eats the plant, which would make it a primary consumer. Also, frogs do not eat plants.
notes.3: This chain ends with a plant eating a frog, which is not possible. A food chain must start with a producer.

why.right: The frog is a secondary consumer when it eats an insect that has eaten a plant.
wrong: The frog is a secondary consumer when it is the second organism written in the chain.
The frog is a secondary consumer when it is eaten by an insect that has eaten a plant.

questions.q: Food webs show
questions.explain: A food web shows how the food chains in an ecosystem are linked, because many organisms eat, or are eaten by, more than one kind of organism.
questions.lo: Identify producers and consumers in a food chain

notes.0: A food web shows consumers as well as producers. Think about how several food chains fit together.
notes.1: One food chain is shown by a single line of arrows. A food web is made of more than that.
notes.2: A food web shows producers and consumers too, not just decomposers. Think about how several food chains fit together.

questions.q: During photosynthesis, plants make food from
questions.explain: During photosynthesis, plants use light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water. Oxygen is given out.
questions.lo: Describe the roles of photosynthesis and respiration in energy flow

notes.0: Oxygen is given out in photosynthesis, not used. Think about the two raw materials plants take in.
notes.2: Oxygen is a product of photosynthesis, and minerals are not used to make glucose. Think about the raw materials plants take in.
notes.3: Oxygen is given out in photosynthesis, not used. Water is one raw material, so think about the gas taken in from the air.

questions.q: Respiration releases energy from food in the presence of
questions.explain: Respiration releases energy from food, such as glucose, using oxygen. Carbon dioxide and water are produced.
questions.lo: Describe the roles of photosynthesis and respiration in energy flow

notes.1: Carbon dioxide is a product of respiration, not something it needs. Think about the gas that is used up.
notes.2: Nitrogen is not used in respiration. Think about the gas we breathe in to release energy from food.
notes.3: Light is needed for photosynthesis, not respiration. Respiration happens in the dark as well.

questions.q: In grass --> goat --> tiger, which organisms carry out respiration?
questions.explain: All living things carry out respiration to release energy from food. Grass, goats and tigers are all living things, so all three respire.
questions.lo: Describe the roles of photosynthesis and respiration in energy flow

notes.1: Every living thing needs energy, not just predators. Think about which organisms are alive.
notes.2: Plants respire too. They release energy from the food they make, day and night.
notes.3: Animals need energy too, so they respire. Respiration is not limited to plants.

why.right: All three organisms respire because every living thing needs to release energy from food.
wrong: All three organisms respire because they all make their own food from sunlight.
All three organisms respire because they all breathe air in through lungs.

questions.q: The energy in a food chain first comes from
questions.explain: Producers trap light energy from the Sun to make food by photosynthesis. This energy then passes along the food chain.
questions.lo: Describe and use the one-way flow of energy through a food chain

notes.0: Heat in the soil is not used by plants to make food. Think about what producers use in photosynthesis.
notes.2: Decomposers feed on dead matter. They do not supply the energy that enters a food chain.
notes.3: Minerals help plants grow, but they are not a source of energy. Think about what producers use in photosynthesis.

why.right: The energy comes from the Sun because producers use light energy to make food in photosynthesis.
wrong: The energy comes from the Sun because animals take in sunlight directly through their skin.
The energy comes from the Sun because sunlight warms the soil and gives plants their food.

questions.q: At each stage of a food chain, about 90% of the energy is
questions.explain: At each stage, most of the energy is used for life processes such as respiration and movement and is lost as heat. Only about 10% passes to the next organism.
questions.lo: Describe and use the one-way flow of energy through a food chain

notes.0: Energy is not returned to the Sun. Think about what happens to energy used in respiration and movement.
notes.1: Only about 10% is passed to the next organism. Think about where the rest goes.
notes.2: The producer is only the first stage. At every stage, most of the energy leaves the food chain.

why.right: Most energy is lost as heat because organisms use it for life processes such as respiration and movement.
wrong: Most energy is lost as heat because organisms store it all and never use any of it.
Most energy is lost as heat because the energy is sent back to the producers.

questions.q: The flow of energy in a food chain is
questions.explain: Energy enters a food chain as light, passes from one organism to the next and is lost as heat. It is not recycled, so the flow of energy is non-cyclical.
questions.lo: Describe and use the one-way flow of energy through a food chain

notes.0: Nutrients are recycled, but energy is not. Energy lost as heat cannot be used again by producers.
notes.1: Producers cannot reuse heat lost from organisms. They need a fresh supply of light energy.
notes.3: Energy decreases at each stage because much of it is lost as heat. It does not increase.

why.right: Energy flow is non-cyclical because energy lost as heat cannot be used again by producers.
wrong: Energy flow is non-cyclical because decomposers return all the energy to the plants.
Energy flow is non-cyclical because energy increases at each stage of the food chain.

questions.q: A producer has 10 000 kJ of energy. About how much reaches the primary consumer?
questions.explain: Only about 10% of the energy passes to the next stage. 10% of 10 000 kJ is 1000 kJ.
questions.lo: Describe and use the one-way flow of energy through a food chain

notes.0: 100 kJ is only 1% of the energy. That is about the amount after two stages, not one.
notes.1: 9000 kJ is about 90%, which is the energy lost as heat. Only a small part passes on.
notes.3: Not all the energy passes on. Most is lost as heat at each stage.

why.right: About 1000 kJ reaches the primary consumer because only about 10% of the energy passes to the next stage.
wrong: About 1000 kJ reaches the primary consumer because about 90% of the energy passes to the next stage.
About 1000 kJ reaches the primary consumer because the energy is shared equally among ten producers.

questions.q: A primary consumer gets 500 kJ. About how much reaches the secondary consumer?
questions.explain: Only about 10% of the energy passes to the next stage. 10% of 500 kJ is 50 kJ.
questions.lo: Describe and use the one-way flow of energy through a food chain

notes.1: 450 kJ is about 90%, which is the energy lost as heat. Only a small part passes on.
notes.2: Not all the energy passes on. Most is lost as heat at each stage.
notes.3: Energy decreases along a food chain. The next stage cannot have more than the primary consumer had.

why.right: About 50 kJ reaches the secondary consumer because only about 10% of the energy passes on.
wrong: About 50 kJ reaches the secondary consumer because about 90% of the energy passes on.
About 50 kJ reaches the secondary consumer because the rest of the energy goes back to the producer.

questions.q: A secondary consumer gets about 200 kJ. About how much did the primary consumer get?
questions.explain: Each stage receives only about 10% of the energy of the stage before. So the primary consumer had about 10 times as much, 10 times 200 kJ, which is 2000 kJ.
questions.lo: Describe and use the one-way flow of energy through a food chain

notes.0: 20 kJ is 10% of 200 kJ, which works the wrong way along the chain. The earlier stage must have had more energy.
notes.2: Adding a little energy does not account for all the energy lost as heat. The next stage receives only a small fraction.
notes.3: The primary consumer comes earlier in the chain, so it had more energy, not less. Most of its energy was lost as heat.

why.right: The primary consumer had about 2000 kJ because only about one tenth of its energy passed on.
wrong: The primary consumer had about 2000 kJ because energy increases tenfold at each later stage.
The primary consumer had about 2000 kJ because about nine tenths of its energy passed on.

questions.q: Decomposers feed on
questions.explain: Decomposers, such as bacteria and fungi, feed on dead organisms and faeces. They break them down into simple substances.
questions.lo: Describe how decomposers recycle nutrients

notes.0: Feeding on living plants is what herbivores do. Decomposers feed on matter that is no longer alive.
notes.1: Feeding on living animals is what predators and parasites do. Decomposers feed on matter that is no longer alive.
notes.2: Light energy is used by producers, not decomposers. Decomposers get their food from the remains of other organisms.

questions.q: The flow of nutrients in an ecosystem is
questions.explain: Decomposers break down dead matter and return nutrients to the soil. Plants take in these nutrients again, so nutrients are recycled and their flow is cyclical.
questions.lo: Describe how decomposers recycle nutrients

notes.0: One-directional describes how energy flows. Nutrients are returned to the soil and used again.
notes.2: Nutrients also pass from plants to animals when animals eat plants. Think about how nutrients get back to the soil.
notes.3: Energy flow is non-cyclical because energy is lost as heat. Nutrients are not lost in this way, and decomposers return them to the soil.

why.right: Nutrient flow is cyclical because decomposers return nutrients to the soil for plants to use again.
wrong: Nutrient flow is cyclical because nutrients are lost as heat at each stage.
Nutrient flow is cyclical because plants make new nutrients from sunlight each day.

questions.q: All decomposers are removed from a forest. What will happen?
choices: nutrients are not returned to the soil
questions.explain: Decomposers break down dead matter and return nutrients to the soil. Without them, dead matter piles up and nutrients are not returned for plants to use.
questions.lo: Describe how decomposers recycle nutrients

notes.0: Plants get nutrients from the soil after decomposers break down dead matter. Without decomposers, this supply would drop.
notes.1: Dead leaves are broken down by decomposers. Without them, the leaves would break down much more slowly.
notes.3: Energy flow is never cyclical, because energy is lost as heat. Removing decomposers affects the cycling of nutrients instead.

why.right: Removing decomposers stops nutrient return because decomposers break down dead matter into nutrients for the soil.
wrong: Removing decomposers stops nutrient return because decomposers make nutrients from sunlight.
Removing decomposers stops nutrient return because decomposers are the producers in a food chain.

questions.q: Motor vehicles harm the environment by
questions.explain: Motor vehicles burn fuels such as petrol, which gives off carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas that adds to global warming.
questions.lo: Evaluate the impact of human activities and technology on the environment

notes.0: Burning fuel uses up oxygen. Vehicles do not give out oxygen.
notes.1: Burning fuel releases heat, and the gases given off trap heat in the atmosphere. Vehicles do not cool the environment.
notes.2: Vehicles give out carbon dioxide when fuel burns. They do not take it in.

why.right: Motor vehicles harm the environment because burning fuel gives off carbon dioxide, which traps heat.
wrong: Motor vehicles harm the environment because burning fuel takes in all the carbon dioxide.
Motor vehicles harm the environment because burning fuel gives off oxygen, which traps heat.

questions.q: A toad brought in to eat beetles also ate many local animals. This shows
choices: introduced organisms can disrupt an ecosystem
toads cannot survive in new habitats
questions.explain: The toad was brought in to eat beetles, but it also ate many local animals. This shows that an introduced organism can upset the balance of an ecosystem.
questions.lo: Evaluate the impact of human activities and technology on the environment

notes.1: The toad changed the ecosystem by eating many local animals. This shows that ecosystems can change.
notes.2: The toad harmed local animals, so introduced organisms do not always help. Think about the effect on the whole ecosystem.
notes.3: The toad survived and spread in its new habitat. That is how it was able to eat so many local animals.

why.right: The toad disrupted the ecosystem because it ate local animals and upset the feeding relationships there.
wrong: The toad disrupted the ecosystem because it made its own food and took sunlight from plants.
The toad disrupted the ecosystem because it ate only the beetles it was brought in to control.

questions.q: Imported food adds to climate change mainly because its transport
choices: burns fuels that give off greenhouse gases
questions.explain: Planes, ships and lorries that carry imported food burn fuels. Burning fuels gives off carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas that adds to climate change.
questions.lo: Evaluate the impact of human activities and technology on the environment

notes.0: Burning fuel uses oxygen. Transport does not give off oxygen.
notes.1: Transport gives off carbon dioxide when fuel burns. It does not take it in.
notes.3: Preservatives keep food fresh, but they are not what releases greenhouse gases. Think about where the energy for long journeys comes from.

why.right: Transporting imported food adds to climate change because burning fuel gives off greenhouse gases.
wrong: Transporting imported food adds to climate change because burning fuel gives off oxygen.
Transporting imported food adds to climate change because the food rots and cools the air.

questions.q: Slowing down climate change helps organisms because it
choices: makes them adapt in one generation
stops them from needing to adapt
questions.explain: Adaptations develop over many generations. If climate change happens slowly, organisms have more time to adapt to the new conditions.
questions.lo: Evaluate the impact of human activities and technology on the environment

notes.0: Adaptations take many generations to develop. They cannot appear within one generation.
notes.1: The climate still changes when the change is slowed, so organisms still need to adapt. Slowing it gives them more time.
notes.2: Slowing climate change does not change the length of food chains. Think about how long adaptations take to develop.

why.right: Slowing climate change helps organisms because adaptations develop over many generations.
wrong: Slowing climate change helps organisms because adaptations develop within a few days.
Slowing climate change helps organisms because adaptations develop only when predators are gone.

questions.q: Some communities wrap food in banana leaves to
choices: make the food last for months
kill all the bacteria on the food
questions.explain: Banana leaves are natural and break down easily. Using them to wrap food reduces the use of plastic, which does not break down easily.
questions.lo: Show awareness of how some cultures practise sustainable living

notes.0: The leaves are only a wrapping and are not eaten. Think about which material the leaves replace.
notes.2: A leaf wrapping keeps food fresh for a short time only. Think about which material the leaves replace.
notes.3: Leaves do not kill all the bacteria on food. Think about which material the leaves replace.

why.right: Banana leaves reduce plastic use because they are a natural wrapping that breaks down easily.
wrong: Banana leaves reduce plastic use because they are made from plastic that has been recycled.
Banana leaves reduce plastic use because they cannot be broken down by decomposers.

questions.q: A community limits how many salmon can be caught each year. This is
questions.explain: Limiting the catch leaves enough salmon to breed and keep the population going. Using a resource without using it up is sustainable living.
questions.lo: Show awareness of how some cultures practise sustainable living

notes.1: Deforestation is the clearing of forests. This example is about fish.
notes.2: Parasitism is a relationship between two organisms. This example is about how people use a resource.
notes.3: Overfishing means catching too many fish. Limiting the catch does the opposite.

why.right: Limiting the salmon catch is sustainable because enough fish are left to breed for the future.
wrong: Limiting the salmon catch is sustainable because salmon breed faster when more of them are caught.
Limiting the salmon catch is sustainable because it removes all the predators of salmon.
